title: ADH / Vasopressin & Cardiac ANF Antagonism
learningObjectives: Explain the hypothalamic osmoreceptor reflex triggering ADH release
Describe the cellular mechanism of Aquaporin-2 channel translocation in the collecting duct
Differentiate Diabetes Insipidus from Diabetes Mellitus
Detail the counter-regulatory natriuretic mechanism of ANF
content:
### 6.2 ADH (Vasopressin) Feedback Loop

```
                      ADH vs ANF HORMONAL ANTAGONISM
                      
   HYPOTHALAMIC ADH (Vasopressin)            CARDIAC ANF (Atrial Natriuretic Factor)
   ├── Secreted during Dehydration/Low Vol   ├── Secreted by Heart Atria during High Vol/BP
   ├── Stimulates H₂O reabsorption via       ├── Causes Vasodilation of renal arterioles
   │   Aquaporin-2 insertion in DCT/CD       ├── Promotes Na⁺ & H₂O excretion (Natriuresis)
   └── Decreases Urine Volume                └── INHIBITS Renin and Aldosterone release
```

- **Hypothalamic Osmoreceptor Trigger**: Dehydration, sweating, or blood loss raises plasma osmolarity ($>300\text{ mOsmol/L}$), stimulating osmoreceptors in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus. Nerve impulses trigger the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) to secrete **Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH / Vasopressin)**.
- **Aquaporin-2 Translocation**: ADH binds basolateral $V_2$ G-protein coupled receptors on collecting duct principal cells $\rightarrow$ cAMP/PKA cascade $\rightarrow$ exocytic insertion of vesicular **Aquaporin-2 (AQP2)** water channels into the apical membrane. Water exits the lumen osmotically into the hypertonic medulla, producing concentrated, low-volume urine.
- **Diabetes Insipidus**: Defective ADH secretion (Neurogenic) or mutated $V_2$ receptors / AQP2 channels (Nephrogenic) causes inability to reabsorb water, resulting in severe **Polyuria ($10\text{--}20\text{ Liters/day}$ of dilute, tasteless urine)** and compensatory Polydipsia (excessive thirst).

### 6.3 Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) Antagonism
- **Trigger**: Excessive venous blood return stretches the walls of the cardiac atria (Hypertension / Hypervolemia).
- **ANF Actions**:
  1. Dilates renal afferent arterioles and relaxes systemic vascular smooth muscle, reducing blood pressure.
  2. **Directly inhibits Juxtaglomerular Renin secretion and Adrenal Aldosterone synthesis**.
  3. Inhibits $\text{Na}^+$ reabsorption in the collecting duct, promoting **Natriuresis** (urinary excretion of sodium) and concomitant water excretion to return blood pressure and volume to normal baselines.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Differential Diagnosis: Diabetes Mellitus vs Insipidus
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Diabetes Mellitus involves insulin deficiency/resistance, resulting in hyperglycemia, glucosuria, ketonuria, and sweet-tasting urine with high specific gravity. Diabetes Insipidus involves ADH dysfunction, resulting in massive excretion of dilute, tasteless (insipid), sugar-free urine with low specific gravity (<1.005).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Alcohol & Diuresis
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Ethanol directly inhibits hypothalamic ADH secretion, preventing Aquaporin-2 insertion and causing pronounced osmotic diuresis and dehydration following alcohol consumption.
